feedback.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\operatorname{sin}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{sin}⁡x-3 & =0 \\ 5\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =3 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡x & =0.6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(0.6)=36.869\,897{…}^{∘}≈{36.870}^{∘}
$$

Since $36.870$ lies inside the range, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={36.870}^{∘}.$

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={36.870}^{∘}.$
Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the second quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={36.870}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13951962/assets/38b2ec0588022556acd825c6b351d572d52034c6ec5cdeddbdff1dbf7baa11a2.png)

A second solution $X$ lies in the $2$nd quadrant, and we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
X={180}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R}={180}^{∘}-{36.870}^{∘}={143.130}^{∘}
$$

Since this value is already inside the required domain, we keep it as our second solution.

So, in ascending order, rounded to one decimal place, the solutions are

$$
x≈{37}^{∘},\,x≈{143}^{∘}.
$$
